title: ZE 155 sheet line – web/R3F model contract
status: planned (not built); revised after review-plan-01 (C1, I1–I10, M1–M7, AD1–AD4) and review-plan-02 (N1–N5)

coordinates.blender_to_three: (x, y, z)_blender -> (x, z, -y)_three; exporter export_yup=True does this
coordinates.origin: unchanged from Blender: X = 0 at the drive-side face of barrel B1, floor at three Y = 0, three -Z = Blender +Y (operator side)
coordinates.axis_rule: Blender rotation +θ about axis a = +θ about three axis M·a (M is a proper rotation). Blender +Y -> three [0,0,-1]

naming.allowed_chars: [a-z0-9_] only. GLTFLoader sanitizes names (removes . : / [ ] and spaces) and suffixes duplicates, so names must already be unique across BOTH files

patterns.part: p_<blender object name> (the Blender copy is named p_<src>, so the source name stays free)
patterns.three_child_meshes: a part with several materials loads as a Group named p_* whose child Mesh objects are named after the glTF MESH (= Blender mesh-data name, made unique), not after the node. userData sits on the Group. Code and check_glb.py must never rely on child names; the registry indexes only nodes that carry userData.kind

naming.mesh_data_names: mesh data of web copies is renamed to the node name (m_<node>) so child meshes read sensibly; never put custom properties on mesh data

hierarchy.line.glb: ze155_line > sec_<group> (10) > dev_<id> (189) > [p_* parts | rot_* > p_* | anim_* > p_*]
hierarchy.interior.glb: ze155_interior > dev_screws (identity) > [rot_screw_a|b > elements, spline shaft, pre-cuts, gbx outputs] + [p_int_fill_screw_*] ; ze155_interior > ih_<host> (identity) > [p_int_* | rot_* > p_* | anim_* > p_*]
hierarchy.runtime_link: no re-parenting. Both roots are rendered side by side (<primitive> each). Every interior node carries userData.device_id = host, so picking walks up to the first ancestor with device_id. A registry Map<device_id, Object3D[]> holds dev_<id> (line) plus ih_<id> (interior) so selection, outline, bbox and swaps cover both files. Animation mixers use their own gltf.scene as root.
rules: mesh nodes are always leaves with a static transform (gltf-transform quantize may rewrite their TRS)
everything that moves (rotors, clips) is an empty (no mesh) with mesh children
device nodes carry translation = device bbox centre (three), no rotation/scale
no node is both a device and a mesh
dev_screws is the one device node with an identity transform (documented exception)

device.note: long texts (function, details, connections) are NOT in extras; they live in devices.json keyed by device_id

part.removed_in_1_1: swap_to (swaps are per state now: cut_states.*.swap)

required.states: string[] (states that may show it; FREE implied for role full, except the nodes in cut_states.FREE.hide)

required.rpm: number (signed, real speed; + = right-handed about axis)

cut_state.where: model-contract.json cut_states (also emitted as build/cut_states.json); not a glTF node

cap.where: runtime material variant, not a glTF node
cap.rule: only for parts with userData.closed = true; open meshes get a DoubleSide lit variant instead

required.name: one of clips[].name
required.targets: node names that exist in the same file

node_kinds.registry_rule: index only nodes with userData.kind (GLTFLoader keeps the raw node name in userData.name); child meshes of multi-material Groups are reached through their Group

excluded_objects.screws_a: replaced by interior int_screw_* (device screws lives in interior.glb)
excluded_objects.ctx_floor: procedural floor material; the web draws its own ground

melt_heater_bands.name: p_melt_heater_bands__<part>
melt_heater_bands.note: assign each loose island to the nearest x

die_body_bolts.by: island bbox-centre Z (Blender, m): > 1.2 top, < 1.2 bottom
die_body_bolts.name: p_die_body_bolts__<part>

die_heater_boxes.by: island bbox-centre Z (Blender, m): > 1.2 top, < 1.2 bottom
die_heater_boxes.name: p_die_heater_boxes__<part>

device_mapping_rules: 1. Blender object name == parts.json id -> that device (177 objects)
2. explicit prefix rules (object_to_device holds the resolved result for all 343 objects)
3. longest parts.json id that is a prefix of the object name
4. 4 synthetic devices: x_ctrl_cabling, x_melt_sensor_cabling, x_takeoff, x_thickness_scanner (A1b anim_ctx_scanner + head)
5. A1b context objects go to line.glb: anim_roll_markers_* under the roll rotors (devices ctx_roll_*), anim_ctx_scanner* (x_thickness_scanner)
Within one device, parts may sit in different ax_* groups; cut rules work per part, selection works per device

rules: a node belongs to exactly one file
clips target only nodes in their own file (same clip name may exist in both)
no textures; no cameras; no lights in the GLBs
W1 is re-runnable: tools/w1_build.py deletes and rebuilds only objects it owns inside scene ze155_web (Đợt 2 re-exports line.glb for die_open and the split wrappers)
files.build/standin/standin.glb: small synthetic contract-shaped GLB (tools/make_standin.mjs, gltf-transform core): 2 sections, 4 devices, parts with userData, 1 rotor, 1 clip, 1 cut state; lets stream B start at t0

not: Draco (needs a decoder from a CDN or a local copy; slower decode)
KHR_meshopt_compression (not read by three-stdlib 2.36 GLTFLoader used by drei useGLTF)
Blender built-in meshopt/draco (keep the raw export inspectable)
forbidden: gltf-transform optimize with defaults (flatten + join + palette destroy the hierarchy and material names)
gltf-transform instance (instanced meshes cannot be animated and lose parents)
compression.global_flag: --vertex-layout separate (plain BufferAttributes for three-mesh-bvh and clipping)

instancing: none in v1. The 64 screw element nodes reference 10 shared glTF meshes (exporter keeps shared data when the copy has no modifiers); GLTFLoader shares the geometry, so memory is shared and draw calls stay at 128.
lod: none. One 18 m machine, mostly viewed close; LOD would only add work. Optional later: gltf-transform simplify on the 10 heaviest parts.

window.__ze: selfcheck(): report (incl. rayUnfiltered: meshes whose raycast is not the filter; must be 0, also under npm run dev)
capCheck(state, device): clicks the screen point of a visible cap/inner face of a clipped device and returns the picked device_id
cutRoundTrip(): {ok, bad[]} – FULL -> FREE -> FULL and every fixed state -> FREE -> same state give the same visible-node set; ok also needs renderer.clippingPlanes empty at the end

closed_test.rule: closed = no boundary edge (edge with 1 face) AND every 2-face edge is contiguous (consistent winding) AND signed volume > 0 (normals out). Edges with 3+ faces (touching shells) are allowed.
closed_test.how: bmesh from the evaluated mesh of the web copy, read only; write userData.closed and log per part; list every part that is clipped in some state and comes out open
closed_test.render_rule: closed -> FrontSide, cap variant DoubleSide with the back-face cap; open or flipped -> DoubleSide lit, no cap; cap "force" lets a nearly closed part (e.g. rolls whose holes are hidden by the journals) use the cap after a visual check

cap_rule: pre-cut parts carry their own cap materials (za_cap_*: steel brick red, screw, gear grey, copper heater, beige insulation, cladding); runtime caps use cap_colors by material class

cut_model.hybrid: fixed teaching states reuse the A1a/A1b pre-cut variants (cut_only) wherever they exist or read better (screw X-sections with shaft disc, _lo fills and head/valve, pump halves, die A-A, layered pipe caps, die lower face); runtime clipping only for FREE and for parts with no pre-cut (barrel hollows, feed column, covers, shells, frames, rolls…)

keys.swap: {exterior node: [interior nodes shown instead]}; the code hides every key and shows the values (values also appear in show_whole or show_clipped)
keys.clip: nodes clipped with the state plane (runtime cap if closed)
keys.show_whole: interior nodes shown unclipped (pre-cuts, whole screws, ghosts, markers)
keys.show_clipped: interior nodes shown and clipped with the state plane
keys.ghost: nodes drawn with GhostMaterial and made non-pickable
keys.peel: runtime peel of clip + swap keys

cut_model.missing_target_rule: if a swap value does not resolve (e.g. Đợt 1 GLB without melt-line items), keep the exterior key visible and clip it instead of hiding it
cut_model.exclusivity: a state never shows two nodes of the same place: full vs cut_only (int_pump_body_hollow vs int_pump_body_cut, gear _full vs halves, exterior vs its pre-cut)
cut_model.cut_rule_used: exterior lists from the shots.json box rule computed on real Blender bboxes, then hand-adjusted for the hybrid (swaps, die_open targets kept, bolt heads hidden in A-A). Split parts (melt_heater_bands__*, die_*__top/bottom) are placed by name; the builder re-checks them with the same rule.
